summary: Yakoma territory (Nord-Ubangi) lies in the far north of the DRC on the Ubangi/Mbomou border with the Central African Republic, far from the eastern conflict zones. No Congolese or foreign armed group is known to hold territory here; the state (PNC in towns and villages, FARDC border/garrison elements, ANR, territorial administration and customary chiefs) is the de facto authority. Risks are cross-border spill-over from CAR (refugees, occasional armed elements, poachers) and ordinary crime, which do not amount to control. All locations are assigned to the PNC by default state presence; web research could not be performed in this run, so confidence is medium for Yakoma town and low elsewhere.

zones.description: Yakoma town (territory seat, GRID3 'Ensien Combatan'/Yakoma cité) on the Ubangi at the Uele-Mbomou confluence
zones.evidence: Territory headquarters with territorial administration, PNC commissariat and FARDC/border-security elements facing the Central African Republic; no armed group is known to hold or tax the town. Insecurity is limited to ordinary crime and cross-border concerns. No web research was possible in this run (search budget exhausted and news/UN sites blocked by the egress proxy), so this rests on default state presence and general background knowledge.

zones.description: Villages of the Yakoma secteur along the Ubangi/Mbomou border with CAR (Kangbua, Ndagba, Sanga, Ngusua, Dongo, Limasa, Kanza, Mbase etc.)
zones.evidence: Riverine border villages opposite CAR's Basse-Kotto/Mbomou prefectures, where CAR armed groups have been active; cross-border spill-over (refugees, occasional armed elements, poaching) has not been reported to amount to territorial control on the DRC side. PNC posts, customary chiefs and FARDC border positions are the default authority. No web research was possible in this run (search budget exhausted and news/UN sites blocked by the egress proxy), so this rests on default state presence and general background knowledge.

zones.evidence: Rural interior of Nord-Ubangi with no known armed-group presence; order is kept by PNC posts at secteur/groupement centres together with customary chiefs, with the FARDC only in larger centres or on patrol.
